title: The Adult Work of Freedom
author: Kathleen Schafer
source: Extraordinarily Ordinary: A Field Guide for Being Human, July 17, 2026
summary: Using childhood memories of exploring woods in Michigan as a metaphor, the author distinguishes between two kinds of freedom: freedom from harmful things, and the deeper freedom to create, contribute, and move toward what is generative. The first kind of freedom — escaping diminishing roles, unhealthy relationships, and limiting expectations — is necessary and dignified, but a life organized only around leaving cannot sustain a meaningful direction. The second kind, 'Desired Contribution' in the Leadership Connection Model, asks what quality of care, creativity, or wisdom wants to move through us into the world. When freedom-from defines a life, 'enough' keeps moving farther away; when freedom-to begins to guide intention, needs can expand without becoming extraction. The adult work of freedom is to become free enough to choose with consciousness, joyful enough to contribute with generosity, and powerful enough to use power in service of life.
points: There are two kinds of freedom: freedom from what diminishes us (old roles, limiting relationships, systems that reduced us) and the deeper freedom to create, contribute, and move toward what is generative.

A life organized only around escape cannot sustain meaning; at some point the question shifts from 'what am I getting away from?' to 'what am I now free to create?' — this is the work of evolved freedom.

Desired Contribution, Step Two in the Leadership Connection Model, asks what quality of care, creativity, strength, vision, or wisdom wants to move through us into the world — a different orientation from pursuing enough.
When freedom from defines a life, 'enough' keeps moving farther away; when freedom to begins to guide intention, our rising doesn't have to require someone else's diminishment.
The adult work of freedom is to become free enough to choose with more consciousness, joyful enough to contribute with more generosity, and powerful enough to use our power in service of life.
quotes: Looking back, I understand those woods as a great gift in the middle of a difficult childhood. At the time, I probably thought of them as an escape — a place the demands of the household couldn’t quite reach, a place where I could breathe.

There are seasons when freedom begins by getting away from what diminishes us. Sometimes distance is the first breath of healing, the first step a person can take before they’re able to hear what they actually want next.
There is a freedom that begins with escape, and there is a deeper freedom that begins to ask where we're going.
A life cannot be organized only around leaving. At some point, if we're fortunate, the question changes. Not only, what am I getting away from but, what am I now free to create?
When freedom from defines a life, there may never be enough. But when freedom to begins to guide our intention, our needs can expand without becoming extraction.
This is the adult work of freedom: to become free enough to choose with more consciousness, joyful enough to contribute with more generosity, powerful enough to use our power in service of life.
